questions.stem: An indexer reports Success, but several known source documents are absent from Search. Where should the investigation start?

options.text: The successful run label and aggregate index document count.
The semantic ranker configuration used by the question-answering application.
The run's document-level errors and warnings.
The service's query-latency dashboard for searches made after the run.

explanation.whyCorrect: Review detailed indexer execution results. A run-level Success status does not establish successful processing of every document.

whyDistractorsWrong.D: Query metrics do not identify failed ingestion items.
whyDistractorsWrong.A: A successful run can still include document-level errors.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: Reranking does not explain documents that failed ingestion.

questions.stem: Complete a backend memory-search tool definition and response header for per-user preferences. user_key is derived from the authenticated session.

options.text: Inspect all slot choices.
Complete the configured fields.

explanation.whyCorrect: The memory tool resolves the placeholder from the memory-user header, falling back to caller TID/OID without it. A backend must supply its authenticated end-user key.

whyDistractorsWrong.scope: Use the documented per-user placeholder; static scope pools users and a title is not a partition key.
whyDistractorsWrong.header: The memory-user header carries end-user identity; a trace ID does not select a user and Authorization identifies the calling service.

questions.statementTemplate:
from azure.ai.projects.models import MemorySearchPreviewTool, PromptAgentDefinition
tool = MemorySearchPreviewTool(memory_store_name="preferences", scope="{{scope}}")
agent = project.agents.create_version(agent_name="support",
    definition=PromptAgentDefinition(model=deployment, tools=[tool]))
response = client.responses.create(input=message,
    extra_body={"agent_reference": {"name": agent.name, "type": "agent_reference"}},
    extra_headers={"{{header}}": user_key})

questions.stem: A supported reasoning model returns a reasoning summary through Responses. A product manager wants to label it 'the model's complete internal reasoning'. Which description is accurate?

options.text: A policy-adherence score produced by an agent evaluator.
An API-provided reasoning summary.
A raw transcript containing each internal reasoning step.
A deterministic execution log for the model's hidden operations.

explanation.whyCorrect: Reasoning summaries are a supported response feature for applicable models. They should not be represented as the full internal reasoning process.

whyDistractorsWrong.C: The summary does not expose all internal reasoning.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: The response is not a complete operational execution log.
whyDistractorsWrong.A: The returned reasoning summary is not an evaluator result.

questions.stem: A support assistant should stay within product support and ask for clarification when evidence is insufficient. Which prompt control expresses both?

options.text: A system-defined domain and missing-evidence fallback.
More tone examples without defining scope.
A low temperature with no role instructions.
A larger retrieval top-k value alone.

explanation.whyCorrect: System messages express role, scope and fallback. Test behavior and apply other mitigations because instructions do not guarantee compliance.

whyDistractorsWrong.C: Temperature affects sampling rather than defining the task boundary.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: Retrieval quantity does not state domain behavior.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: Examples of tone do not replace an explicit scope/fallback contract.

questions.stem: A deterministic workflow sends a request to a retrieval specialist and then a policy specialist. What must its orchestration represent?

options.text: One larger model context replacing all flow rules.
Separate trace IDs with no shared request context.
Explicit specialist handoff and completion conditions.
Tool descriptions treated as executable routing code.

explanation.whyCorrect: Multi-agent orchestration needs explicit workflow control and termination conditions. Distinct specialist roles do not themselves supply a valid process.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: Context size does not define routing or completion.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: Descriptions are not the orchestrator’s executable flow.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: Uncorrelated telemetry makes diagnosis harder and does not define completion.

questions.stem: An agent calls the translation tool for a request that requires stock availability. The translation call is valid and succeeds. Which evaluation pinpoints the mistake?

options.text: Tool Call Success.
Tool Output Utilization.
Tool Selection.
Tool Input Accuracy.

explanation.whyCorrect: Tool Selection measures whether the selected tool is appropriate. A valid and successful invocation can still be the wrong tool for the task.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: Execution success is not the same as choosing the right tool.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: The scenario says the call was valid.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: Output use is downstream of choosing the wrong capability.
